---
title: "Reading the outputs"
subtitle: "What a run wrote, where, and whether it is still current"
---

Everything a run produces lands under the `project_dir` named in the config.
Nothing is written back into the toolbox repository.

## The layout

```
<project_dir>/
  config/
    basin_data/                  copies of basin inputs that live outside the repo
    runs/                        what each run was configured with (below)
      build_model/
      analyze_projections/
      invocations/               one immutable manifest per wrapper invocation
      journal.jsonl              append-only ledger, two lines per executed run
  data/
    spatial/geoms/               region, basins, subbasins, rivers, locations
    spatial/plots/               the basin map and its companions
    climate/historical/          the climate store, per source and window
    climate/projections/cmip6/   the CMIP6 slices and derived change factors
  models/
    hydrology/wflow/             the model: config, forcing, staticgeoms,
                                 run_default (the historical run), evaluation
  experiments/<name>/            ONE stress test, self-contained:
    config/                      including the model reference it is bound to
    climate/weathergenr/         the generated and perturbed weather realizations
    hydrology/wflow/             the runs across the perturbation grid
    results/                     the hydrological indicators — the response surface
  logs/                          one log per workflow
  benchmarks/                    one benchmark table per workflow
```

The organising rule: artifacts sit under **who produced them** and **which
engine** they belong to, so you can tell what made a file from where it sits.
An experiment is a self-contained partition — two experiments never share a
directory, and neither can overwrite the other's results.

## Logs and benchmarks

Each workflow writes exactly one log and one benchmark table, both regenerated
on every run:

| Workflow | Log |
|---|---|
| `analyze_climate.smk` | `logs/wf0_analyze_climate.log` |
| `build_model.smk` | `logs/wf1_build_model.log` |
| `analyze_projections.smk` | `logs/wf2_analyze_projections.log` |
| `run_stress_test.smk` | `logs/wf3_run_stress_test_<experiment>.log` |

All four land in the project's own `logs/`, so one run's records sit side by
side. The stress test is experiment-scoped, so its log and benchmark table carry
the experiment id in the **filename** — the `experiments/<name>/` subtree holds
only that experiment's own inputs and products.

While a workflow runs, individual rules log into `logs/_parts/` (one level
deeper for the stress test, so two experiments can never merge each other's
parts). A final rule merges the parts into the single log — one
`== W.NN  rule_name` section per rule — then deletes them. Benchmarks work the
same way, into `benchmarks/wf<N>_benchmarks.md`.

## Provenance: what a run was configured with

Each workflow writes a **`run_record.yml`**:

- `<project_dir>/config/runs/build_model/run_record.yml`
- `<project_dir>/config/runs/analyze_projections/run_record.yml`
- `<exp_dir>/config/run_record.yml`

The record is **current-only** — it describes the most recent run and is
replaced, not accumulated. It carries the toolbox commit (and whether the
checkout was dirty), the environment lock-file hashes, the source config's
digest, the resolved advanced settings, and one entry per referenced external
input.

A referenced file is **copied into the project only when the toolbox repository
cannot give it back**. A catalog or template that lives in the checkout, is
tracked and is unmodified is recorded by its git blob id instead — duplicating
what version control already holds serves nobody.

### The two digests answer different questions

| Digest | Covers | Use it to ask |
|---|---|---|
| `effective_config_sha256` | the settings the workflow was asked to run under | did the *configuration* change? |
| `configuration_inputs_sha256` | the above, plus the toolbox commit, the lock files, and the bytes of every referenced catalog and template | did this run see the same configuration-side inputs as that one? |

Compare runs with the wide one; the narrow one moves only when settings move.
Only the keys a workflow actually reads enter its digests, so editing the
stress-test section does not invalidate the model-build record.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Neither digest covers scientific data identity

A remote or mutable dataset can change under an unchanged catalog entry without
moving either digest. Configuration provenance is not data provenance.
:::

### The journal

`<project_dir>/config/runs/journal.jsonl` is the append-only ledger: two lines
per run sharing an `invocation_id`, recording start and outcome. One journal per
project; stress-test lines name their experiment.

It records **executed** runs. A Snakemake invocation that finds everything up to
date does no work and appends nothing — so a gap in the dates means nothing
needed doing, not that nobody looked.

## Are these outputs current?

Compare the sidecar written beside the outputs with the workflow's run record:

| Outputs | Sidecar, relative to `project_dir` |
|---|---|
| model build | `models/hydrology/wflow/evaluation/run_metadata.json` |
| stress test | `experiments/<name>/results/run_metadata.json` |
| projections | `data/climate/projections/<clim_project>/summary/provenance.json` |

A `configuration_inputs_sha256` in the sidecar that differs from the run
record's means **the outputs predate the recorded configuration**. The journal
then names the runs on either side.

For the model build specifically,
`models/hydrology/wflow/hydromt_build_config.yml` records the values HydroMT was
*actually handed* — which is not the same as the build template, because
arguments are replaced with the spatial products the earlier stage produced and
some are derived at call time.
